mode.label: Mode
mode.about: Historical keeps every structure label (BOS / CHoCH) the indicator has found. Present shows only the most recent ones, so the chart stays clean.
mode.example: Scrolling back a week to study how gold trended → Historical. Live scalping where only the current structure matters → Present.

style.label: Style
style.about: Color theme for the structure drawings. Colored uses the bullish/bearish colors you pick below; Monochrome draws everything in grays.
style.example: Monochrome is useful when you also run other colorful indicators and want SMC structure to stay in the background.

show_trend.about: Paints the candles with the internal structure trend: bullish color while structure is bullish, bearish color while it is bearish. A filled candle closed with the trend; a hollow candle is a pullback.
show_trend.example: Gold breaks internal structure up at 2,610 → candles turn the Bullish Structure color (blue) until a bearish break turns them yellow.

aoi_max_dist.about: Hides zones far outside the recent range (highest high to lowest low of the last 120 bars). Zones more than this number × that range above the high or below the low are hidden. 0 turns the filter off.
aoi_max_dist.example: Recent range 2,560–2,600 (40 points) and 0.2 → zones above 2,608 or below 2,552 are hidden.

show_internals.about: Shows internal (minor) market structure: the small BOS and CHoCH breaks inside the bigger swing.
show_internals.example: On a 5m chart this marks the small breaks you would scalp; turn it off to see only the major swing structure.

show_ibull.about: Which bullish internal breaks to draw, and their color. BOS = break of structure (trend continues). CHoCH = change of character (trend flips).
show_ibull.example: Choose CHoCH to see only the first bullish break after a downtrend, the typical early reversal signal.

show_ibear.about: Which bearish internal breaks to draw, and their color. BOS = trend continues down. CHoCH = the trend flips from up to down.
show_ibear.example: Choose BOS to see only bearish continuation breaks while gold is already falling.

ilength.about: How many bars on each side confirm a minor (internal) swing high or low. Smaller = more, faster swings; larger = fewer, cleaner swings. It is always kept below Swing Length.
ilength.example: 5 → a high counts as an internal swing once 5 bars on its right fail to go above it.

ifilter_confluence.about: Ignores weak internal breaks. A bullish break only counts when the breakout candle closes in the upper half of its range (bearish: lower half), so wick fakeouts are skipped.
ifilter_confluence.example: A candle spikes above the high to 2,615 but closes near its low at 2,606 → with the filter on, no BOS is drawn.

show_Structure.about: Shows swing (major) market structure: the main BOS and CHoCH breaks of the larger trend.
show_Structure.example: On the 1H chart this shows the trend a day trader follows; internal structure shows the smaller moves inside it.

show_bull.about: Which bullish swing breaks to draw, and their color. BOS = trend continues up. CHoCH = the trend flips from down to up.
show_bull.example: All shows both. CHoCH only highlights the moment the higher-timeframe trend turned bullish.

show_bear.about: Which bearish swing breaks to draw, and their color. BOS = trend continues down. CHoCH = the trend flips from up to down.
show_bear.example: Pick CHoCH to be alerted visually only when the major uptrend breaks.

show_swings.about: Labels swing points HH / HL / LH / LL. The number is the Swing Length: how many bars on each side confirm a major swing point.
show_swings.example: Length 25 on 15m → a swing high needs 25 bars (about 6 hours) on its right that stay below it. HH = higher high, LL = lower low.

show_hl_swings.about: Marks the latest strong and weak highs and lows. A weak high is likely to be taken out (liquidity); a strong high protects the trend.
show_hl_swings.example: In an uptrend the latest high is Weak (target above it) and the low that started the move is Strong (break below = trend in doubt).

show_iob.about: Shows internal order blocks: the last opposite candle before a move that broke internal structure. The number is how many of the nearest ones to keep.
show_iob.example: 3 → only the 3 internal order blocks closest to the current price are drawn.

show_ob.about: Shows swing order blocks: the last opposite candle before a move that broke swing structure. The number is how many of the nearest ones to keep.
show_ob.example: A bullish swing OB at 2,588–2,592 is where price may bounce on a retest after the break.

ob_filter.about: How very large (volatile) candles are kept from becoming order blocks. Atr compares the candle to ATR(200); Cumulative Mean Range compares it to the average range so far, which works better with little history.
ob_filter.example: A news candle 3× the normal size is skipped as an OB source, so the block is not oversized.

ob_candle.about: Which candle becomes the order block. Opposite Candle (ICT): the last down candle before a bullish displacement (up candle before a bearish one). Extreme Candle (LuxAlgo): the candle with the lowest low / highest high of the leg.
ob_candle.example: ICT style: three red candles then a big green displacement breaks structure → the last red candle is the bullish OB.

ob_disp_mult.about: ICT mode only. The breakout candle must have a body at least this many ATR(14) in the break direction to count as displacement.
ob_disp_mult.example: ATR = 4 points and value 1.0 → the displacement candle body must be at least 4 points.

ibull_ob_css.about: Fill color of internal bullish order blocks. Keep it transparent so candles stay visible.

ibear_ob_css.about: Fill color of internal bearish order blocks.

bull_ob_css.about: Fill color of swing bullish order blocks.
bull_ob_css.example: A darker blue than internal OBs, so major blocks stand out.

bear_ob_css.about: Fill color of swing bearish order blocks.
bear_ob_css.example: A darker red than internal OBs.

show_eq.about: Marks equal highs (EQH) and equal lows (EQL): two highs or lows at almost the same price. Stops tend to sit beyond them, so they act as liquidity targets.
show_eq.example: Two highs at 2,631.2 and 2,631.5 → EQH line; price often runs above it to take stops before reversing.

eq_len.about: How many bars confirm each high/low used for equal-high/low detection.
eq_len.example: 5 → each of the two highs needs 5 bars on its right that stay below it.

eq_threshold.about: How close two highs (or lows) must be to count as equal, as a fraction of ATR. Lower = stricter, fewer but better matches.
eq_threshold.example: ATR = 5 points and 0.1 → highs within 0.5 point count as equal.

show_fvg.about: Shows fair value gaps: a 3-candle imbalance where candle 1 and candle 3 do not overlap. Price often comes back to fill them.
show_fvg.example: Candle 1 high 2,600, candle 3 low 2,604 → a bullish FVG box from 2,600 to 2,604.

fvg_auto.about: Skips small gaps. The middle candle of the gap must move (open to close, in %) more than twice the average candle move so far.
fvg_auto.example: Average candle move 0.05% → only gaps whose middle candle moved more than 0.10% (about 2.6 points at 2,600) are drawn.

fvg_tf.about: Timeframe used to find fair value gaps. Chart = the current timeframe. A higher timeframe shows its gaps on your chart; a lower one falls back to the chart timeframe.
fvg_tf.example: Trading on 5m with Timeframe 1H → you see the 1H gaps, which are stronger levels.

bull_fvg_css.about: Fill color of bullish fair value gaps.

bear_fvg_css.about: Fill color of bearish fair value gaps.

fvg_extend.about: How many bars the FVG boxes reach past the current bar.
fvg_extend.example: 5 → each gap box ends 5 bars to the right of the latest candle.

fvg_extend_active.about: Keeps unfilled gaps stretched to the current bar. A gap is removed once price fills it completely.
fvg_extend_active.example: Off → each gap stays only as wide as its 3 candles; on → it follows price until filled.

fvg_max_active.about: Maximum unfilled gaps kept on each side (bullish and bearish). Older ones are removed first.
fvg_max_active.example: 5 → at most 5 bullish and 5 bearish open gaps on the chart.

show_pdhl.about: Draws the previous day's high and low (PDH / PDL) with the line style and color you pick.
show_pdhl.example: Yesterday's high was 2,624 → a PDH line at 2,624, a common target and reaction level.

show_pwhl.about: Draws the previous week's high and low (PWH / PWL).
show_pwhl.example: Last week's low 2,571 → a PWL line; a sweep below it and a quick reclaim is a classic ICT setup.

show_pmhl.about: Draws the previous month's high and low (PMH / PML). Needs at least one completed month of data in the feed.
show_pmhl.example: Last month's high 2,685 → a PMH line far above, a long-term target.

show_sd.about: Shades premium (top), equilibrium (middle) and discount (bottom) of the current swing range. ICT idea: buy in discount, sell in premium.
show_sd.example: Swing range 2,560–2,620 → above 2,590 is premium, below 2,590 is discount.

premium_css.about: Color of the premium zone (upper part of the range, expensive prices).

eq_css.about: Color of the equilibrium zone (around the 50% level of the range).

discount_css.about: Color of the discount zone (lower part of the range, cheap prices).

ds_mode.about: How demand/supply distances are measured. ATR: multiples of ATR(14), adapts to volatility and works on every timeframe. Percent: fixed percentages of price (the original settings).
ds_mode.example: ATR is recommended for gold: 1 ATR is about 1.5 points on 1m and about 30 points on 1D, so one setting fits both.

ds_min_atr.about: ATR mode. A demand/supply zone is created once price moves away from the base candle by at least this many ATRs.
ds_min_atr.example: ATR = 4 points and 2.0 → price must run 8 points away from the base candle to create a zone.

ds_max_atr.about: ATR mode. Zones taller than this many ATRs are trimmed toward the base candle.
ds_max_atr.example: ATR = 4 and 1.0 → a zone is at most 4 points tall.

ds_line_atr.about: ATR mode. Lines are shown for active zones within this many ATRs of the close.
ds_line_atr.example: ATR = 4 and 10 → only zones within 40 points of price get a line.

ds_min_pc_change.about: Percent mode. Minimum % move away from the base candle to create a zone.
ds_min_pc_change.example: 0.05% of 2,600 = 1.3 points; a rally of at least 1.3 points creates a demand zone.

ds_max_pc_zone.about: Percent mode. Maximum zone height as a % of price; taller zones are trimmed toward the base candle.
ds_max_pc_zone.example: 0.05% of 2,600 → zones at most 1.3 points tall.

ds_line_pc_display.about: Percent mode. Lines are drawn for active zones when the close is within this % of them. Max line = how many lines per zone type.
ds_line_pc_display.example: 3% and Max line 3 → up to 3 demand and 3 supply lines, only for zones within 3% (about 78 points) of price.

ds_max_zones.about: Maximum stored zones per type. The oldest tested or invalidated zones are removed first.
ds_max_zones.example: 100 → up to 100 demand and 100 supply zones kept in history.

ds_hours_offset.about: Hours added to the times shown in zone label tooltips, for when you read times in a zone other than UTC.
ds_hours_offset.example: You are in Cambodia (UTC+7) → set 7 so a zone shows 21:00 instead of 14:00.

showDemandZone.about: Shows demand zones (areas where buyers pushed price up) with their border and background colors. Solid = fresh, dotted = tested by a wick, dashed gray = invalidated by a close below.
showDemandZone.example: Gold rallies hard from 2,575 → a demand zone at the base; the first retest is the classic buy area.

showSupplyZone.about: Shows supply zones (areas where sellers pushed price down) with their border and background colors. Solid = fresh, dotted = tested by a wick, dashed gray = invalidated by a close above.
showSupplyZone.example: Gold drops sharply from 2,630 → a supply zone at the base; the first retest is the classic sell area.

dsAlertDemand.about: Which zone types raise alerts: Hit (price touches an active zone) and Near (price approaches it). Alert conditions are calculated but not yet delivered anywhere in this app.
dsAlertDemand.example: Only Demand on → you would be alerted when price falls into or near a demand zone, never for supply.

ds_alert_mins_no_repeat.about: Minutes to wait before repeating the same alert for the same zone. 0 turns this off; max 120.
ds_alert_mins_no_repeat.example: 60 → if price keeps poking the same zone, you get at most one alert per hour for it.

ds_alerts_pc_near.about: Percent mode. A Near alert fires when the high or low is within this % of a zone. Max 5%.
ds_alerts_pc_near.example: 1.5% of 2,600 = 39 points away counts as near.

ds_near_atr.about: ATR mode. A Near alert fires when the high or low is within this many ATRs of a zone.
ds_near_atr.example: ATR = 4 and 1.0 → within 4 points of the zone counts as near.

left.about: Bars to the left that a pivot must beat to become a support/resistance zone. Higher = fewer, more important pivots.
left.example: 20 → a high must be the highest of the previous 20 bars.

right.about: Bars to the right that must confirm the pivot. Higher = more reliable but appears later.
right.example: 10 on 15m → a pivot is confirmed 10 bars (2.5 hours) after it formed.

nPiv.about: How many pivot highs and lows are tracked at the same time.
nPiv.example: 2 → the latest 2 resistance and 2 support zones are kept.

atrLen.about: Bars used to average the ATR that sets the zone width, so zones look similar across timeframes.

mult.about: Zone thickness as a multiple of ATR.
mult.example: ATR = 6 points and 0.5 → each zone is 3 points tall.

per.about: Maximum zone height as a % of price, to stop huge zones during very volatile moves.

max.about: How many candle-pattern boxes are kept. More pattern boxes leave fewer drawing slots for pivot zones far back in history.
max.example: 10 → only the latest 10 pattern boxes stay on the chart.

fut.about: How many bars to the right of the last candle the price-level labels are placed.
fut.example: 30 → level labels sit 30 bars to the right, in the empty space after the latest candle.

src.about: Which prices form the pivots. High/Low Body: candle bodies (ignores wicks). High/Low: full wicks. HA: smoothed Heikin-Ashi bodies.
src.example: Gold often wicks through levels → Body ignores those spikes and gives tighter zones.

alignZones.about: Merges a new zone into an existing one when their edges overlap, so a level that holds again and again becomes one stronger zone.
alignZones.example: Support at 2,580–2,583 forms again at 2,582–2,585 → one zone that gets brighter each time it holds.

extend.about: Extends current pivot zones to the right edge of the chart.
extend.example: On → today's support box keeps going right so you can see it as price approaches.

lLab.about: Shows price labels on the key-level lines extended off pivot zones.
lLab.example: A label reading 2,602.40 at the right end of a resistance line.

dhighs.about: Tracks pivot highs (resistance). Off = no resistance zones are created.
dhighs.example: Turn off when you only want to see support below price.

dlows.about: Tracks pivot lows (support). Off = no support zones are created.
dlows.example: Turn off when you only want to see resistance above price.

detectBO.about: Arrow below the bar when price breaks above ALL tracked pivots: a strong breakout.
detectBO.example: Close at 2,632 above every tracked resistance → breakout arrow.

detectBD.about: Arrow above the bar when price breaks below ALL tracked pivots: a strong breakdown.
detectBD.example: Close at 2,548 below every tracked support → breakdown arrow.

breakUp.about: Arrow when price closes above a resistance zone.

breakDn.about: Arrow when price closes below a support zone.

falseBull.about: Bear trap: price closes below support, then quickly closes back above it. Often leads to a fast move up.
falseBull.example: Close at 2,576 under support 2,580, next bar closes at 2,584 → false-breakdown arrow.

falseBear.about: Bull trap: price closes above resistance, then quickly closes back below it. Often leads to a fast move down.
falseBear.example: Close at 2,616 over resistance 2,613, next bar closes at 2,609 → false-breakup arrow.

supPush.about: Triangle under up candles that form inside a support zone: support is holding.
supPush.example: A green candle closes inside support 2,580–2,583 → triangle below it.

resPush.about: Triangle over down candles that form inside a resistance zone: resistance is holding.
resPush.example: A red candle closes inside resistance 2,610–2,613 → triangle above it.

curl.about: Marks a TSI momentum 'curl' (momentum turning) while price is inside a key zone, a hint that the move is changing direction.
curl.example: Price sits in support and TSI turns up → bullish curl triangle.

repaint.about: Wait for the candle to close before detecting patterns. Off shows possible patterns while the candle is still forming, and they may disappear.
repaint.example: On → a hammer only appears after its candle closes, so it never vanishes.

labels.about: Shows a text label with the name of each detected candle pattern.
labels.example: A label 'Bullish Engulfing' under the candle.

sBox.about: Draws a box around each detected candle pattern.
sBox.example: A green box around the two candles of a bullish engulfing.

d_.about: Detects doji candles: a tiny body with wicks on both sides, showing indecision.

be_.about: Detects engulfing patterns: the second candle's body fully covers the previous candle's body in the opposite direction.
be_.example: Red candle 2,605→2,600, then green 2,599→2,607 → bullish engulfing.

hs_.about: Detects hammers (long lower wick, small body at the top) and shooting stars (long upper wick, small body at the bottom).
hs_.example: Range 2,590–2,602 with the body at 2,600–2,602 → hammer.

dg_.about: Detects dragonfly doji (long lower wick, no upper wick) and gravestone doji (long upper wick, no lower wick).
dg_.example: Open = close = high = 2,600, low 2,594 → dragonfly doji.

tw_.about: Detects tweezer tops and bottoms: two candles with almost the same high (top) or low (bottom), in opposite colors.
tw_.example: Two candles both with a low of 2,580.3 → tweezer bottom.

st_.about: Detects spinning tops: a small body in the middle with similar wicks above and below.
st_.example: Body 2,600–2,601 in a 2,596–2,605 range → spinning top.

pc_.about: Detects piercing line (green closes above the middle of the previous red) and dark cloud cover (red closes below the middle of the previous green).
pc_.example: Red 2,610→2,600, then green 2,598→2,606 (above the 2,605 midpoint) → piercing.

bh_.about: Detects harami: a small candle whose body sits inside the previous large body.
bh_.example: Big red 2,620→2,600, then small green 2,604→2,608 → bullish harami.

ls_.about: Detects candles with a very long upper or lower shadow (wick), a sign of rejection.
ls_.example: Range 2,590–2,610 with the body at the bottom 2,590–2,592 → long upper shadow.

alertMode.about: When pattern alerts would fire: once per bar (as soon as it appears, may change before close) or once per bar close (confirmed only).
alertMode.example: once_per_bar_close avoids alerts for patterns that disappear before the candle closes.

ecWick.about: Engulfing candles must cover the previous candle's wicks too, not only its body. Stricter.
ecWick.example: On → the engulfing candle's range must also exceed the previous high and low.

colorMatch.about: Hammers must be green candles and shooting stars must be red. Stricter, fewer signals.
colorMatch.example: On → a red hammer is no longer counted.

closeHalf.about: Tweezer patterns must close beyond the middle of the previous candle.
closeHalf.example: On → a tweezer bottom needs the second candle to close above the first candle's midpoint.

atrMax.about: Ignores pattern candles bigger than this many ATRs (for example news spikes). 0 turns it off.
atrMax.example: ATR = 5 and 3.0 → candles longer than 15 points are not used for patterns.

rejectWickMax.about: Engulfing: the largest wick allowed on the confirming candle, as a % of its body. 0 turns it off.
rejectWickMax.example: 50 → a confirming candle with a 4-point body may have at most a 2-point wick against the move.

hammerFib.about: Hammers and stars: the body may be at most this % of the whole candle.
hammerFib.example: 33 → a 12-point candle may have at most a 4-point body.

hsShadowPerc.about: Hammers and stars: the opposite wick may be at most this % of the body.
hsShadowPerc.example: 5 → a hammer with a 4-point body may have at most a 0.2-point upper wick.

hammerSize.about: Hammers, stars and long shadows must be at least this many ATRs long, to skip tiny candles.
hammerSize.example: ATR = 5 and 0.1 → the candle must be at least 0.5 point long.

dojiSize.about: Doji: the body may be at most this % of the whole candle.
dojiSize.example: 5 → a 10-point candle counts as a doji with a body of 0.5 point or less.

dojiWickSize.about: Doji: one wick may be at most this many times the other, so the doji stays balanced.
dojiWickSize.example: 2 → bottom wick 3 points, top wick 1 point is rejected (3× is more than 2×).

luRatio.about: Long shadow: the wick must be at least this % of the whole candle.
luRatio.example: 75 → in a 20-point candle the long wick must be 15 points or more.

lookback.about: Maximum bars between a close beyond a zone and the close back inside it, for false-break signals. Wick-only sweeps do not count.
lookback.example: 2 → close below support, then a close back above within 2 bars = false breakdown.

swing.label: Swing High/Low
swing.about: Swing size used to filter breakout-type signals. Higher = only more significant swings, so fewer signals.
swing.example: 5 → a breakout must clear a swing confirmed by 5 bars on each side.

reflect.about: A pattern only counts near a significant high or low within this many bars (max 250).
reflect.example: 10 → a hammer counts only if it is at, or near, the lowest low of the last 10 bars.

offset.about: How close to the extreme the pattern candle must be. 0 = must be the highest/lowest bar; 1 = can be the next one.
offset.example: 1 → a hammer one bar after the actual low still counts.

bullBorder.label: Bullish levels
bullBorder.about: Border and background colors of bullish key levels (support zones).
bullBorder.example: Light blue border with an almost transparent fill.

bearBorder.label: Bearish levels
bearBorder.about: Border and background colors of bearish key levels (resistance zones).
bearBorder.example: Light yellow border with an almost transparent fill.

upCol.label: Breakout / breakdown
upCol.about: Colors of the breakout (up) and breakdown (down) arrows.
upCol.example: Orange for breakouts, magenta for breakdowns.

supCol.label: Resistance / support break
supCol.about: Colors of the resistance-break (up) and support-break (down) arrows.
supCol.example: Green when resistance breaks, red when support breaks.

fBull.label: Bear trap / bull trap
fBull.about: Colors of the false-break arrows (bear trap, bull trap) and their maximum height in pixels.
fBull.example: Green / red arrows, at most 75 px tall.

moveBullCol.label: Off support / resistance
moveBullCol.about: Colors of the triangles for candles reacting off support (bullish) and resistance (bearish).
moveBullCol.example: Purple under candles bouncing from support, yellow over candles rejected at resistance.

curlBullCol.label: Bullish / bearish curl
curlBullCol.about: Colors of the bullish and bearish TSI momentum-curl markers.
curlBullCol.example: Green for a bullish curl, yellow for a bearish curl.

patBullBg.label: Backgrounds
patBullBg.about: Background colors of candle-pattern boxes: bullish, neutral, bearish.
patBullBg.example: Very transparent green / gray / red so the candles stay readable.

patBullBo.label: Borders
patBullBo.about: Border colors of candle-pattern boxes: bullish, neutral, bearish.
patBullBo.example: Slightly stronger green / gray / red than the background.

textBullCol.label: Text
textBullCol.about: Text colors of pattern labels: bullish, neutral, bearish.
textBullCol.example: Bright green text for 'Hammer', gray for 'Doji', red for 'Shooting Star'.

labBullCol.label: Label background
labBullCol.about: Background colors of pattern labels: bullish, neutral, bearish.
labBullCol.example: Transparent green / gray / red behind the label text.

strat.about: TSI speed preset for the momentum-curl detection. Fast reacts sooner (more signals); Slow is smoother (fewer, later signals).
strat.example: Scalping on 1m–5m → Fast. Swing trading on 1H+ → Slow.

longf.about: Fast preset: long smoothing length of the TSI.

shortf.about: Fast preset: short smoothing length of the TSI.

signalf.about: Fast preset: signal-line length. A curl is the TSI turning relative to this line.

longs.about: Slow preset: long smoothing length of the TSI.

shorts.about: Slow preset: short smoothing length of the TSI.

directions.about: Shows the direction dashboard: one row per indicator (MACD, Stoch RSI, Vortex…) saying buy or sell. Context only, not entry signals.
directions.example: 8 of 9 rows say 'sell' → momentum broadly agrees the market is bearish.

infoDataTableOn.label: Direction table
infoDataTableOn.about: Turns the whole direction (الاتجاه = 'direction') table on or off.
infoDataTableOn.example: Off frees space on the chart but keeps the calculations running.

itablePosition.label: Position
itablePosition.about: Where the direction dashboard sits on the chart.
itablePosition.example: top_right keeps it away from the newest candles, which are at the bottom right when price is falling.

macdOn.about: Shows the MACD row in the dashboard. MACD above its signal line = buy, below = sell.

macdOrder.about: Row position of this indicator in the dashboard (1 = top). To move a row, swap the numbers of two indicators.
macdOrder.example: Set MACD to 3 and Vortex to 1 → Vortex moves to the top, MACD to row 3.

stochasticOn.about: Shows the Stochastic RSI row in the dashboard. Adds OB/OS when it is overbought (above 80) or oversold (below 20).
stochasticOn.example: K at 85 and falling → 'Stoch sell OB'.

stochasticOrder.about: Row position of Stochastic RSI in the dashboard (1 = top).

smoothK.about: Smoothing of the Stochastic RSI K line.

smoothD.about: Smoothing of the D line (the average of K). Used only by the 'K vs D' direction rule.

stochDirectionMode.about: How the Stoch RSI direction is decided. K vs 50: K above 50 = buy. K vs D: K above D = buy (reacts faster).
stochDirectionMode.example: K = 60, D = 70 → 'K vs 50' says buy; 'K vs D' says sell.

lengthRSI.about: RSI length used inside the Stochastic RSI.

lengthStoch.about: Stochastic length applied to that RSI.

vortexOn.about: Shows the Vortex row. VI+ above VI- = buy, below = sell.

vortexOrder.about: Row position of Vortex in the dashboard (1 = top).

momOn.about: Shows the Momentum row: close minus the close N bars ago. Positive = buy, negative = sell.
momOn.example: Close 2,600 vs 2,590 ten bars ago → +10 → 'Mom buy'.

momOrder.about: Row position of Momentum in the dashboard (1 = top).

momLength.about: How many bars back Momentum compares the close with.
momLength.example: 10 → compares with the close 10 bars ago.

rsiOn.about: Shows the RSI row. RSI above 50 = buy, below 50 = sell; OB above 70, OS below 30.
rsiOn.example: RSI 28 → 'RSI sell OS' (bearish but oversold, so a bounce is possible).

rsiOrder.about: Row position of RSI in the dashboard (1 = top).

psarOn.about: Shows the Parabolic SAR row. Close above the SAR dots = buy, below = sell.

psarOrder.about: Row position of PSAR in the dashboard (1 = top).

psarInc.about: How much the acceleration grows each time a new extreme is made.

psarMax.about: Maximum acceleration factor. Higher = the SAR catches up with price faster.

dmiOn.about: Shows the DMI row. DI+ above DI- = buy, below = sell; shows 'wait' while ADX is below the threshold.

dmiOrder.about: Row position of DMI in the dashboard (1 = top).

adxThreshold.about: DMI shows 'wait' while ADX (trend strength) is below this level. 0 = always show a direction.
adxThreshold.example: 20 → in a flat market with ADX 15 the row says 'wait' instead of buy or sell.

mfiOn.about: Shows the Money Flow Index row: an RSI that weights each bar's typical price (H+L+C)/3 by its volume. Above 50 = buy, below 50 = sell; OB above 80, OS below 20.
mfiOn.example: MFI 62 → 'MFI buy'. With no volume data the row says 'no volume'.

mfiOrder.about: Row position of MFI in the dashboard (1 = top).

fisherOn.about: Shows the Fisher Transform row. Rising = buy, falling = sell.

fisherOrder.about: Row position of Fisher in the dashboard (1 = top).

recommendation.about: Shows BULB buy/sell labels at RSI extremes: buy when RSI leaves oversold, sell when it leaves overbought. It is a counter-trend exhaustion marker, not an entry signal: on XAUUSD 1H/4H (2025–2026) the move after BULB labels was no better than average, and sell labels in the 2025 uptrend were followed by further rises. Use it with structure and zones, not on its own.
recommendation.example: RSI(13) drops below 30 → a 'buy' label under that candle.

bulbMode.about: Fixed (confirmed), the default: the label prints once, on the bar where RSI closes back out of overbought/oversold, and never moves. Moving (original): the label keeps jumping to newer, more extreme bars while RSI stays extreme, so history shows the exact top or bottom, which was not knowable at the time (it repaints).
bulbMode.example: RSI goes above 65 at 10:00 and peaks at 10:45. Fixed: 'sell' appears when RSI drops back below 65 and stays there. Moving: 'sell' first appears at 10:00, then slides to the 10:45 high.

rsiOverbought.about: RSI level above which BULB prints a sell.
rsiOverbought.example: 65 → RSI 67 prints 'sell'. Raise to 70 for fewer, stronger signals.

rsiOvesold.about: RSI level below which BULB prints a buy.

bulbAlternate.about: Fixed mode only. Allows a sell only after a buy (and the reverse), so a strong trend does not print many signals against it.
bulbAlternate.example: In a strong downtrend you get one 'buy', then nothing until a 'sell' appears.

mal.about: Length of the SMA in the middle of the ATR bands.
mal.example: 47 → the blue middle line is the 47-bar average close.

atrl.about: ATR length used for the band distance.

atrm.about: Band distance from the SMA, in ATRs. Higher = wider bands.
atrm.example: ATR = 4 and 3.0 → bands 12 points above and below the SMA.

bandWidth.about: Line thickness of the SMA and ATR bands, in pixels.
